item.title: ISLAND HISTOY: Kauai centenarian William Kuwalu was born on Niihau in 1849
item.description: William Kuwalu (1849-1953), the son of Waikaka and Kikaha, was born on Niihau on Jan. 26, 1849, raised and educated at Waimea, Kauai, where he later made his home, and was employed for many years by Gay &Robinson Co.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Family sanctuaries worth examination
item.description: Senate Bill 2563, authorizing the use of government-sanctioned city, state, federal or private land for secured temporary shelters serving homeless women and children under age 18, aims to fill a gap that’s not currently met by other services. The need is urgent, and the state Legislature must act to support this goal.

item.title: Hawaii Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke stays silent on state subpoenas
item.description: Twelve days after Hawaii’s attorney general said she issued multiple subpoenas and completed interviews in a criminal investigation born out of a federal political bribery case, Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke will not say if she has been subpoenaed by state investigators.

item.description: LIHUE — The Kauai Police Department (KPD) is requesting the public’s assistance in locating a woman who was reported missing.

item.title: ERSOY: Your liver’s cholesterol thermostat: What it really does (and what actually changes ldl)
item.description: Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance your body needs to function. It’s a building block for every cell membrane, it helps your body make steroid hormones (like estrogen and testosterone), it’s used to produce vitamin D, and it’s required to form bile acids that help you digest and absorb fats.
